message: [DRG-19] Sprint 1 planning at 10:00. Focus: repository, dependencies, the LCL loader. Standups here in writing by 09:45 each day, no meeting.
[DRG-22] Sprint 1 review. Scaffold, dependency tiers and the loader are done; the licence question is still open and blocks how we plan the synthetic work.

Retro. Kept: agreeing the definition of done before writing code. Changed: the RAID log gets reviewed in planning rather than when something breaks. Tried: written standups, which everyone prefers to a call.
[DRG-24] Standup. Yesterday: LCL aggregate statistics for the calibration targets. Today: same, handing them to Divya. No blockers.
[DRG-24] Yesterday: canonical frame. Today: synthetic generator shape. Blocked on the calibration targets, unblocked this morning.
[DRG-26] Yesterday: dependency tiers merged. Today: config and logging utilities.
[DRG-23] Sprint 2 review. Synthetic generator, CLI skeleton and config are in. The licence answer landed today and it reshapes the plan rather than blocking it.
Sprint 3 planning. Data contract, neighbourhood aggregation, CI and the architecture document.
[DRG-30] Sprint 3 review. CI is live and already caught a stale-file dependency. Architecture document is drafted with the non-goals in section two.
[DRG-32] Standup. Yesterday: profiling setup. Today: daily and weekly load shapes for all four sites. No blockers.
[DRG-33] Sprint 4 review. Load shape profiling and household heterogeneity done. The heterogeneity finding is going straight into the simulation design assumptions.
[DRG-1] Sprint 5 review. Seasonal decomposition, the forward-fill bug fixed, and container images. Data foundations epic closes here.
[DRG-40] Sprint 6 review and Q1 close. Six sprints, no forecast, and that was the plan.

[DRG-40] Q1 review done. Question from the stakeholder session, recorded because it will come back: 'when do we see a forecast?' Answer is Q3, and the reason is that a forecast built on data with two corrupt days a year and forward-filled gaps would have been ready in March and wrong.
[DRG-40] That framing helped in the room. Worth reusing verbatim.
[DRG-44] Sprint 7 planning. Feature engineering starts: calendar, cyclical, lags. The split contract is in this sprint too and I want it merged before any model exists.
Sprint 7 review. Calendar features, lags at 1/48/336 and the split contract are in.
[DRG-46] Sprint 8 review. Rolling statistics landed and immediately produced our first leakage bug, caught before anything was published.
[DRG-46] Retro. The useful item: Geetha was suspicious of a good number and that is what caught it. We cannot rely on that indefinitely - action is to turn it into an assertion, which is now in.
[DRG-50] Sprint 9 review. Weather features and lagged temperature in. RAID reviewed - PyTorch moved to active.
Sprint 10 review. Feature sanity pass and the processed dataset materialisation. Feature engineering is effectively complete.
[DRG-52] Sprint 11 planning. The model ladder starts. Order is deliberate: naive, then linear, then trees.
[DRG-53] Sprint 11 review. Both naive baselines published and named separately after the label bug.
[DRG-58] Standup. Yesterday: Ridge results. Today: looking at why test scores are not degrading relative to validation, which they should be.
[DRG-58] Yesterday: processed dataset materialisation. Today: same, plus whatever Geetha finds.
[DRG-55] Sprint 12 review. Ridge at 0.83 against naive at 1.54, and the evaluation harness is the thing that makes those comparable.
[DRG-58] Sprint 13 review. Second leakage bug found and fixed. Two in three months, both caught by suspicion rather than by a test.

[DRG-58] Retro. Action carried from May, now with more urgency: the leakage class needs to be structurally impossible, not merely watched for. Divya has restructured so transforms fit inside the pipeline.
[DRG-59] Sprint 14 review. XGBoost at 0.70 MAE. The headline number of the project so far, and it is more than twice as good as the operational baseline.
Sprint 15 review. Hyperparameter search done, and the finding that it bought very little is worth as much as the tuning.
[DRG-61] Sprint 16 review. Rolling-origin CV confirms the headline sits at the pessimistic end of the fold range.
[DRG-63] Sprint 17 review. Model artefacts now carry their provenance, which is the groundwork for next year's MLOps epic.
[DRG-65] Standup. Yesterday: LSTM training loop. Today: blocked - torch will not import on this machine despite installing cleanly.
[DRG-65] Picking that up. It is the MSVC runtime, which is RAID risk 2 arriving on schedule.
[DRG-4] Sprint 18 review. Deep models evaluated and not adopted, PyTorch risk realised and mitigated, torch-free fallback in. Model ladder epic closes.
Sprint 19 review. Ladder written up. Stress detection starts next sprint.
[DRG-68] Sprint 20 review. Per-site percentile thresholds in, with the wording about what stress does and does not mean carried into every artefact.
[DRG-69] Standup. Yesterday: stress event detection. Today: stress-alarm F1 numbers look wrong across the board - the naive baseline is scoring too well.
[DRG-69] Sprint 21 review. Third leakage bug, this one in the stress threshold. The team has proposed a standing rule rather than a third individual fix.

[DRG-69] Retro, and the honest version: three leakage defects this year, all caught by a person being suspicious. That is a resourcing signal as much as a process one and I am taking it to the year-end review.
Sprint 22 review. Stress events, frequency and duration metrics in.
[DRG-5] Sprint 23 review. Stress-alarm F1 published for every model. Stress detection epic closes.
[DRG-74] Sprint 24 review and year close. EV adoption sampling and charging profiles landed; heat pumps carry into January.
Sprint 27 planning, first of 2026. Scenario engine and the combined EV and heat pump case. RAID review after.
[DRG-80] Standup. Yesterday: scenario engine review. Today: the combined scenario peak equals the sum of the parts, which should not happen physically.
[DRG-80] On it. If the loads are adding exactly then something in the aggregation has lost the time offsets.
[DRG-80] Sprint 28 review. The scenario engine landed and immediately produced a result that looked wrong, which turned into the diversity finding.
[DRG-81] Sprint 29 review. Scenario sweep and peak amplification metrics, with ADMD printed per scenario for auditability.
[DRG-6] Sprint 30 review. Stress under scenarios, and the reporting artefacts that carry the finding. Electrification epic closes.
Sprint 31 review. Replay engine and the carbon intensity feed.
[DRG-88] Sprint 32 review. Replay determinism bug fixed, feed degradation handled. External dependency risk moves from delivery risk to documented behaviour.
[DRG-89] Sprint 33 review. Simulation handover notes signed off by acceptance test - Geetha ran the sweep from the document. Knowledge concentration risk closed.
[DRG-91] Sprint 34 review. Sensitivity framework and the stress sensitivity results.
[DRG-92] Sprint 35 review. Sensitivity written up. The headline is that the conclusion is robust to everything except adoption rate, which we do not forecast and say so.
[DRG-93] Sprint 36 review. SHAP global drivers, and the dashboard shell with its chart theme.
[DRG-97] Sprint 37 review. Stress-period SHAP, the scaling bug fixed, and the demand and forecast page.
[DRG-98] Sprint 38 review. API forecast endpoint in. Neha starts Monday and the onboarding is ready.
[DRG-99] Standup, day two. Yesterday: environment and a full pipeline run. Today: reading the modelling notes and starting the gap analysis.
[DRG-99] Sprint 39 review. Neha's first sprint, and her gap analysis is the most useful document produced this quarter.

Retro. Kept: giving the new joiner a narrow first-week goal and asking for a written finding rather than agreement. Changed: QA reviews contracts before implementation, which already happened on the API and worked.
[DRG-104] Sprint 40 review. Stress, scenario and explanation endpoints, model registry, and the scenario comparison page - which is the page that carries the whole project finding.
[DRG-110] Standup. Yesterday: dashboard smoke tests. Today: found that switching neighbourhood does not change the series - raising it now.
[DRG-107] Standup. Yesterday: gate wired into the retrain. Today: the overnight retrain produced a better-MAE model and the gate refused it, which needs a decision rather than a fix.
[DRG-14] Sprint 41 review. Promotion gate live, SHAP page, and the data and feature regression pack. Engineering practice epic closes.
[DRG-107] Sprint 42 review. Azure infrastructure deploys clean. The gate blocked its first promotion, which everyone agrees is a success rather than an incident.
[DRG-115] Standup, day two. Yesterday: objectives table and the architecture document. Today: stakeholder conversations with network planning.
[DRG-115] Sprint 43 review. AML training job, cost pass, the replay page, and Amit's first week. Three joiners in fifteen months and the onboarding pattern is now settled.
[DRG-124] Sprint 44 planning. Managed endpoint, scheduled retrain, simulation regression pack, BRD refresh and traceability. Monitoring stays blocked on the ownership decision.
[DRG-125] Standup. Yesterday: runbook wording with the planning group. Today: same. The 'what it does not mean' section is taking longer than the rest, which is probably correct.
Standup. Sprint 44, day seven. Reminder that the October steering agenda needs the monitoring ownership decision - DRG-124 is blocked on a rota, not on work.
[DRG-125] Yesterday: reviewing the operator runbook wording. Today: same, plus the stress explanation panel. No blockers.
[DRG-122] Yesterday: replay page polish. Today: starting the sensitivity page, which Amit's traceability work surfaced as the one requirement with a test and no view.
[DRG-113] Yesterday: endpoint scores against the sample request. Today: the verification script, then the traffic shift. Scheduled retrain is running nightly and the gate is deciding.
[DRG-120] Yesterday: sampling, determinism and threshold stability assertions all green. Today: ADMD range checks, then UAT scenarios.
[DRG-119] Yesterday: BRD refresh, two thirds through. Today: traceability - twenty-one of twenty-six traced. Blocked on nothing.
[DRG-126] Standup. Sprint 44 day eight. Reminder: October steering needs the monitoring ownership decision and the probabilistic forecast question that Amit has had raised twice.
[DRG-122] Yesterday: started the sensitivity page. Today: same. No blockers.
[DRG-121] Yesterday: ADMD range checks. Today: finishing those, then UAT scenario scripts.
[DRG-119] Yesterday: traceability to 21 of 26. Today: the remaining five and the BRD refresh.
[DRG-113] Yesterday: endpoint verification script. Today: traffic shift, then the retrain schedule review.
